correctness.rationale: Exact edge-open packing definition checked against 2022 and 2026 primary originals, including the permitted selected star edges. A complete forbidden-pair table yields 37 admissible triples and a 17-state transition graph for all n>=4. The explicitly stated 0/1 potential makes n minus packing size exactly the number of unit-slack arcs. An exact standard-library integer certificate verifies every one of the 37 arc inequalities, A^8=A^2, and six base trace values, proving all residue classes. The triangular prism is handled separately. Independent brute enumeration over all candidate edge subsets for n=3..8 reproduces all cases, but is not used to extrapolate beyond those orders.

evidence: Brešar et al., Section 5, Corollary 5.3, presents general product lower bounds, not a full circular-ladder optimum-count classification.
Das and Santra, arXiv:2610.02275, Theorems 4, 8 and 13 are class-wise computational algorithms, not the exact formula or multiplicity here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A procedure able to calculate an optimum on input is not itself a mathematical statement of the uniform residue-class sizes and counts. General product lower bounds do not fix the sharp circular closure cases, and none of the inspected results implies the exact 6/4n/2n multiplicity partition.

evidence: Filomat 2023 gives 3 colour classes when 6 divides the circumference and 4 otherwise for lengths at least 6, along with small cases 3–5; it supplies no exact maximum colour-class counts.
The 2024 Cartesian-product lower bound uses factor packing and independence numbers, not a phase-counting transfer for the prism.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: At multiples of six, a known three-colouring and a new upper bound can jointly certify existence of an n-edge class, so scalar existence there must not be claimed independent of that implication. But neither such an implication nor the other published statements gives exactly six distinct n-edge sets, the n−1 threshold for all remaining residues, or the 2n/4n counts. The full enumerator and its exact transfer certificate are the claim being assessed.

evidence: The Filomat 2023 prism theorem computes the minimum number of injective-edge-colouring classes for each cycle length; a largest individual class is a different optimisation invariant.
The 2022 defining paper equates edge-open packing with induced star forests; the same invariant is not ordinary induced matching.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The theorem is phrased and checked both as maximum edge-open packing and as maximum injective-edge-colouring colour-class size. In a prism, induced matching is strictly more restrictive because multiple incident edges can form an allowed star. The inspected injective-index theorem determines neither the exact largest single class for nonmultiples of six nor the number of classes attaining this maximum.

originality.rationale: The full primary descriptions and relevant proof sections of four close sources were compared by mathematical implication. The 2023 injective-index theorem gives a related scalar colour count, and the 2024 product results give inequalities, but neither controls the distinct maximum colour classes. No inspected source states the exact 6/4n/2n classification; novelty remains best-knowledge and historically qualified.
residual_risks: Complete historical-priority verification against all papers, databases and unpublished versions has not been performed.
An undiscovered earlier treatment of the exact circular-ladder optimum multiplicities under injective edge-colouring terminology could cover this claim.
Generic exact algorithms could compute finite instances but have not been shown to imply the closed all-length enumerator in any inspected source.

value.rationale: The graph family is canonical in product graph theory and injective edge colouring; the question is a natural precise optimum-set counting problem for a recently active packing invariant. The result isolates an arithmetic six-periodic rigidity threshold, characterises its exceptional six optimum phases and proves linear enumerators in other congruence classes. This is more than a table lookup or a numerical lower-bound substitution and supplies exact benchmarks for algorithms and robustness questions. The scientific value rests on structural and counting information, not an unproved downstream theorem.
